Read about the nursery

Plant care

Repotting, in four steps

01

Wait for roots

Repot when roots show through the drainage holes, not on a calendar. Most plants want it every second spring.

02

Go up one size

12 cm to 17 cm, not 12 cm to 22 cm. A pot too large holds water the roots cannot reach and rots them.

03

Keep the depth

Same soil line as before. Burying the stem is the commonest way to lose a plant to a repot.

04

Water, then wait

Water it in, then leave it a fortnight before feeding. New compost has everything it needs.

title: Plant care
content:
Plant care

Light first, then water

Nearly every houseplant that dies indoors is either in the wrong light or being watered on a schedule that ignores the season.

Light

How we file them

Light, honestly described

Every plant is filed by the light it actually needs, not the light it will tolerate for a month before it gives up.

Water on a schedule you can keep

The card in the box says how often, in weeks, for the room you bought it for. No misting rituals.

Pet safe, marked plainly

Filter the shop to what is safe around a cat or a dog. The rest carry a warning on the label.

A rough guide

How often to water

Spider plant, philodendron

When the top 5 cm is dry, about weekly in summer

Cacti and succulents

Every three to four weeks, none in midwinter

Ferns and fittonia

Keep just moist, never let them dry out

Aloe, echeveria, haworthia

Soak and drain, every three weeks

Every plant, in winter

Roughly half as often as summer

Every second spring

Repotting, in four steps

01

Wait for roots

Repot when roots show through the drainage holes, not on a calendar. Most plants want it every second spring.

02

Go up one size

12 cm to 17 cm, not 12 cm to 22 cm. A pot too large holds water the roots cannot reach and rots them.

03

Keep the depth

Same soil line as before. Burying the stem is the commonest way to lose a plant to a repot.

04

Water, then wait

Water it in, then leave it a fortnight before feeding. New compost has everything it needs.

Something wrong?

Yellow lower leaves usually mean too much water. Crisp brown edges usually mean air that is too dry. Send us a photograph and we will tell you which.

title: The nursery
content:
The nursery

A glasshouse, and four months of patience

We grow what we sell, which takes longer and is the entire difference.

2016

We started because the plants we bought kept dying

Most houseplants are grown fast in Dutch glasshouses, shipped in a warm lorry and sold within a week. They look perfect and then collapse in an ordinary room. We buy plugs and grow them on slowly in our own light, so what leaves here is already used to it.

  • Grown on for at least four months
  • Peat-free compost, always
  • Pots and plants packed in paper, never plastic
Shop the nursery

Four steps

How a plant gets here

01

Plugs

We buy small, from three growers we have visited, and never from a middleman who cannot name the nursery.

02

Four months

They grow on in our glasshouse, in British light, with the heating off from April.

03

Hardened

A fortnight in an unheated room before they are listed, which is where the weak ones show.

04

Packed

In paper, with a care card written for the room you said you were buying for.

title: FAQ
content:
Help

Questions we are asked most

Choosing, delivery, and what to do in the first fortnight.

Choosing

Stand where the plant will go at noon and hold your hand up. A sharp shadow is bright light, a soft one is medium, no real shadow is low. Every plant here is filed by that.

Filter the shop by pet safety. The spider plant, the ferns, the fittonia, the echeveria and the haworthia are all safe; the rest carry a warning on the label.

The 12 cm is a desk or a sill, the 17 cm is a side table, the 22 cm is a floor plant. Pot sizes are the diameter across the top.

Delivery

Wrapped in paper with the pot bagged so the compost stays in. Plants leave on Monday and Tuesday so nothing sits in a depot over a weekend.

Send a photograph within 48 hours. A creased leaf is usually cosmetic and will grow out; anything worse and we replace it.

After it arrives

Probably not. A few leaves after a move is normal while it adjusts to your light. Leave it somewhere stable for a fortnight before doing anything.

When roots come through the drainage holes, usually every second spring. Go up one pot size only.

For the first thirty days. If it fails in that time, tell us and we replace it.

title: Delivery and returns
content:
Delivery and returns

Plants travel on Mondays

Nothing living goes into the post on a Thursday, because nothing living should spend a weekend in a depot.

What it costs

Delivery

Standard delivery

$7, plants leave Monday and Tuesday

Free delivery

On orders over $60

Pots and care only

$4, sent any working day

Collection

Free, from the glasshouse on Friday or Saturday

First month

If a plant fails within 30 days we replace it

Returns

Pots, compost and feed can go back unopened within thirty days. Plants are living things, so they cannot be resold once they have left: if something is wrong with one, we replace it rather than asking for it back.

The first month

If a plant fails within thirty days, send a photograph and we will send another. It happens, usually to a batch rather than a plant, and we would rather know.

Damaged in the post

Photograph the box and the plant within 48 hours. Creased leaves usually grow out and we will say so; a snapped stem gets a replacement.
